claims.event: Wang Zan of Guancheng impressed Shizong of Zhou with legal reasoning, served as deputy commissioner of the Three Departments and Guest Bureau commissioner, was sent by Taizu to Yangzhou and drowned at Chang Bridge.

Commissioner who could not answer Shizong on garrison grain and bore a grudge against Wang Zan.
Rebel whose suppression early in Jianlong led to Wang Zan being sent to rebuild Yangzhou.
Song ruler who sent Wang Zan to Yangzhou, mourned him, and indulged the obstinate Zhao Pin.
Zhang Baoxu, styled Siguang, served six dynasties for forty years in gate protocol, carrying missions to Jingnan and Wu-Yue, and became Commandant of the Guards under the Song.
Father of Zhang Baoxu, senior general of the Tang Left Martial Guard.
Led an army against the Khitan invasion in the second year of Kaiyun.

Opponent whose suppression Zhang Baoxu took part in.
Led his troops out to surrender at Shouzhou to the Later Zhou.
Target of the campaign during which Zhang Baoxu was left at Henei.
Zhao Pin of Danzhou surrendered his city to the Zhou, served as prefect of several prefectures and Director of the Imperial Clan, and was demoted after falsely accusing Zhao Pu over timber trading.
Shu ruler who appointed Gao Yanchou military commissioner of Qinzhou.
Military commissioner of Qinzhou for Shu who fled back after defeat and was refused entry by Zhao Pin.
Ordered early in Xiande to lead an army against Qin and Feng.
Chancellor whom Zhao Pin accused of private timber trading; he was cleared and later interceded for Pin.
Reported with others that Zhao Pin had falsely accused a senior minister.
Subject of the biography heading that follows Zhao Pin’s.

claims.event: Lu Huaizhong of Hejian advised Zhou Taizu on taking Hezhong, reconnoitred Jiangling for Taizu, oversaw the vanguard infantry in the Jing-Hu campaign, and served as prefect of Jiangling and guest-relations commissioner.
Rebel at Hezhong who sent Wang Jixun to hold Tong Pass and attack the stockade west of the river.
Besieged Li Shouzhen’s city, received Lu Huaizhong’s advice and recommended the surrendered Wang Jixun as palace attendant.
Campaigned against at Yanzhou with Lu Huaizhong taking part.
Sent Lu Huaizhong to reconnoitre the route of his northern campaign.
Song ruler who sent Lu Huaizhong to survey Jiangling and later saw through Ding Deyu’s charges against Li Xuan.
Son of Lu Huaizhong, granted appointment as collator in Dazhong Xiangfu 4.
Wang Jixun of Pinglu fought for Li Shouzhen, surrendered to Zhou Taizu, governed several prefectures, urged the conquest of Lingnan and was nicknamed “Wang Three Irons”.
Defeated Wang Jixun at Tong Pass.
Brought his army to the walls of Hezhong against Li Shouzhen.
Brought his army to the walls of Hezhong against Li Shouzhen.
Li Shouzhen’s favourite general, sent with Wang Jixun on the night attack west of the river.
Killed in battle in a border action for which Wang Jixun was demoted.
Southern Han ruler who repeatedly raided across the border into Daozhou.
Ding Deyu of Linming served in gate posts, fought in Jing-Hu and Chenzhou, suppressed Shu bandits, denounced Zhang Yantong and Li Xuan, and was demoted to Fangzhou after Qian Chu reported his abuses.
Father of Ding Deyu, military commissioner of the Zhangwu Army.
Led the pacification of Jing and Hu in which Ding Deyu took part.
Captured Chenzhou together with Ding Deyu and Yin Chongke.
Captured Chenzhou together with Ding Deyu and Pan Mei.
Gate deputy commissioner who fought Shu bandits with Ding Deyu and was executed after Deyu denounced him.
Bandit chief captured by Ding Deyu and Zhang Yantong and torn apart in the market.
Transport commissioner accused by Ding Deyu of seditious drunken talk, punished only for drunkenness and demoted.
Wu-Yue ruler who reported Ding Deyu’s abuses to the throne.

claims.event: Zhang Yantong of Lucheng, overseer of troops in Xichuan, confronted Ding Deyu over his misconduct, was denounced by him and executed for answering Taizu defiantly in Kaibao 2.
Father of Zhang Yantong, senior general of the Later Zhou Right Golden Crow Guard.
Song ruler who sent Zhang Yantong, Ding Deyu, Wang Ban and Zhang Yu to Shu, executed Yantong, and agreed to Liang Jiong’s request to exclude Hanlin academicians from banquets.
Inner Guest Relations commissioner in Shu who resented Zhang Yantong and accused him of sedition.
Reception deputy commissioner garrisoned in Shu, arrested with Zhang Yantong, flogged and exiled to Xuzhou.
Inner attendant in Shu whom Ding Deyu named as Zhang Yantong’s accomplice; flogged and exiled to Shamen Island.
Inner attendant flogged with Zhang Yu and Wang Ban and sent to the Western Kiln Office.
Liang Jiong of Liaocheng served Shizong of Zhou from his princely days, supervised garrisons, fought at Caishi and Taiyuan, defended Yin and Xia against Li Jiqian and died at Yinzhou.
Later Zhou ruler whom Liang Jiong served while still a prince and who promoted him after succeeding.
Prefect of Shuzhou appointed deployment commissioner for Qinzhou, with Liang Jiong supervising his army.
Led troops with Liang Jiong to defeat the Bing invaders.
Led infantry to Jingnan with Liang Jiong and later fortified Bingzhou at Sanjiao with him.
Led infantry ahead to Jingnan with Liang Jiong and Pan Mei in the Jinling campaign.
Song ruler under whom Liang Jiong oversaw the Office of Foreign Affairs, and who restored Hanlin academicians to banquets at Su Yijian’s request.
Wu-Yue ruler whom Liang Jiong welcomed in the Huai and Si region when he came to court.
Garrisoned Dingzhou with Liang Jiong and Cui Han.
Garrisoned Dingzhou with Liang Jiong and Meng Xuanzhe.
Raided the frontier, lured and killed Cao Guangshi, and was opposed by Liang Jiong at Yin and Xia.
Chief inspector lured and killed by Li Jiqian.
Hanlin academician who persuaded Taizong to restore academicians’ seats at banquets.

Father of Shi Gui, commandant of the Jin Yanwei Guard.

claims.event: Taizu’s informant who abused his influence, failed to slander Liang Mengsheng, relieved famine at Guangzhou, dredged the Huimin Canal and died after Cao Bin’s Youzhou campaign.
Song ruler who trusted Shi Gui’s inquiries, curbed his market prosecutions by edict and promoted Liang Mengsheng.
Prefect of Dezhou acting at Xingzhou whose kinsmen were restrained by Liang Mengsheng and who sought Shi Gui’s help to remove him.
Directorate of Education aide governing Dezhou who curbed Guo Gui’s kinsmen; Taizu praised him and made him Left Assistant.
Military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army ordered with Shi Gui to assault Taiyuan’s north wall.
Led dozens of Jianghuai people as outlaws until captured by Shi Gui.
Led the Yongxi campaign against Youzhou in which Shi Gui served.
Native of Ruyin in Yingzhou, son of Tian Lingfang.
Father of Tian Qinzuo, Later Han regimentation commissioner of Guozhou, who seduced Jing Bianting’s wife.
Performer in Tian Lingfang’s household whose wife Lingfang seduced.

claims.event: Tian Qinzuo served Shizong at Huainan, fought in Shu, against Bing, the Khitan and Jiangnan, routed Yang Ye at Hongdong, drove Guo Jin to suicide, and died on the eve of the Youzhou campaign.
Murdered Tian Lingfang by night and fled to join Zhao Sixuan before being routed at Tong Pass.
Murdered in his prefectural office by Jing Bianting.
Rebel whom Jing Bianting fled to join.
Later Zhou ruler under whom Tian Qinzuo was overseer of the vanguard at Huainan.
Shu ruler whose surrender Tian Qinzuo reported to the court.
Commander alongside whom Tian Qinzuo repelled the Bing raid on Leping.
Cavalryman who gave Tian Qinzuo his own horse at Suicheng.
Led cavalry to Jiangling with Tian Qinzuo and Li Hanqiong at the start of the Jiangnan campaign.
Led cavalry to Jiangling with Tian Qinzuo and Cao Bin.
Wu commander beheaded by Tian Qinzuo at Lishui.
Taiyuan commander routed by Tian Qinzuo at Hongdong County.
Song ruler who rewarded Tian Qinzuo with five thousand taels of silver.
Commander with a distinguished battle record who hanged himself after repeated humiliation by Tian Qinzuo.
Commissioner of the Southern Bureau appointed battle-array commissioner with Tian Qinzuo.

claims.event: Hou Yun of Taiyuan managed Guanzhong grain supply for thirty years, governed Jian’an, Yangzhou, Xuzhou and Fuzhou, inspected the Zhe stores after Qian Chu’s surrender, and held Lingzhou for over ten years.
Father of Hou Yun, Later Han prefect of Liaozhou.
Song ruler who moved Hou Yun to Fuzhou, trusted Wang Wenbao, and promoted Di Shousu.
King of Wu-Yue who surrendered his territory, came to court, and was welcomed by Di Shousu.
Wang Wenbao of Yangwu supervised Quanzhou troops, suppressed bandits, oversaw the failed canal project, led troops at Tongyuan and spent thirty years in palace service trusted by Taizu and Taizong.
Surrendered Zhang and Quan prefectures to the Song.
Commissioner of the Six Residences Office who supervised part of the canal works with Wang Wenbao.
Supervised a section of the canal works with Wang Wenbao.
Song ruler who trusted Wang Wenbao.
Di Shousu of Rencheng carried reports on the Shu campaign, settled tribal disputes, crushed the Meishan rebels, burned the Bao Hanyang letters, governed Hangzhou and Henan.
Father of Di Shousu, chamberlain of the Left Palace Guard under the Jin.
Prefect of Haizhou who besieged Fenzhou with Di Shousu supervising his forces.
Eastern Upper Gate commissioner, deputy to Di Shousu in Jiannan.
Military commissioner of Qi to whom Di Shousu was sent as credential envoy.
Defense commissioner of Mingzhou who led a deep raid into Taiyuan territory with Di Shousu.
Rebel leader whose correspondence with officials and rich men Di Shousu burned.

claims.event: Rebuilt the Hebei walls after Liu Tingrang’s defeat, governed Daming, Luzhou and Fengxiang, garrisoned Xiazhou against Jiqian, and served four dynasties for over fifty years; praised for not striving rashly.
Defeated at Junzi Lodge, leaving the Hebei fortifications in ruins.
Toured the Hebei region with Di Shousu to rebuild city walls.

Xia commander who reported his younger brother Jiqian’s incitement of the tribes and requested reinforcements.
Wang Shen, styled Miquan, garrisoned Tongcheng, fought at Xuanzhou, replaced frontier adjutants, captured Zhe Yuye, and was dismissed after goading Yang Ye to his death.
Father of Wang Shen, Privy Councilor under the Later Zhou, whose home Shizong visited after his death.
Visited Wang Pu’s home after his death and appointed Wang Shen Eastern Head palace attendant.
Served with Wang Shen as joint administrator of Chizhou.
Song ruler who sent Wang Shen to replace frontier troops, campaigned in Hedong, and pitied Liu Shenqiong.
Leader of the Hexi Three Clans who joined Li Jiqian and was captured by Wang Shen.
Received the rebel Zhe Yuye.
Goaded by Wang Shen, fought to the death and fell in battle.
Passed the jinshi examination and rose to Doctor of the Grand Temple.
Younger brother of Wang Pu, Right Remonstrator and Historiography Institute historian, later transport commissioner of Guangnan.
Liu Shenqiong of Fanyang served Liu Ci and Taizu, refuted Zheng Shen’s false accusation against Li Chongju, supplied Taizong’s Hedong campaign, and lived past eighty.
Seized power, after which Liu Shenqiong left his service and joined Liu Ci.
Military commissioner of the Yongxing Army who entrusted Liu Shenqiong with responsibility.
Took Liu Shenqiong into his service as a military commissioner and appointed him palace guard after taking the throne.
Privy Councilor falsely accused by Zheng Shen of taking gold from Xi Aisou.
Li Chongju’s follower who struck the Denunciation Drum to accuse him falsely.
Man of Taiyuan alleged to have bribed Li Chongju for the top examination rank.
Hanlin academician alleged to have colluded with Li Chongju.
Praised by the commentators for rising from the ranks and restraining wrongdoing without fear.
Praised by the commentators for never failing on his missions.
Praised by the commentators for foreseeing Jingzhou’s peril.
Praised by the commentators for seeing that Panyu could be taken.
Praised by the commentators for long administering the frontier.
